claims.answer: CLI and MCP address the same canonical issue records for reads, creation, edits, claims, state, dependencies and artifacts. Relayed agents have worker capability scoped to their issue subtree, with --outside-scope confirmation for other existing issues. attachSession is not subtree-gated, but direct rehoming from a real issue is refused and an agent attach naming a Proposed target is refused. That does not make every Proposed subtree inert: operator attachment or spawn-time cwd binding can leave a session attached to a Proposed issue; newSubissue without targetId then bypasses the proposed-parent guard, creates a human-audience backlog child and attaches the existing session. This path remains at v0.3.0 source and was not exercised live. Concurrent-edit handling remains unknown.

questions.question: Permissions
questions.answer: Viewer, worker and admin issue roles exist. A relayed agent receives worker/subtree scope, or none without an issue; --outside-scope confirms other existing-issue writes. Delete and restore are operator-only; only the user closes a decision issue. attachSession is not subtree-gated, but real-issue direct rehoming is refused. Its Proposed guard only checks a supplied targetId for constrained callers. Operator attachment is allowed from a draft session; spawn can persist a Proposed issue attachment through a qualifying cwd when mayJoinIssue passes, because soleOwnerForCwd has no stage filter. Given that attachment, newSubissue with no targetId and confirmRehome creates a human-audience backlog child and attaches the session, bypassing registry create protections. This is a source path, not a verified live exploit.

newSubissue does not spawn another process. It attaches the existing session to a human-audience backlog child, which is why it cannot be described as universally inert. Other active sessions may require a replacement coordinator.
The confirmInterrupt close guard does not fix the proposed-parent attach path. Concurrent-edit handling and attribution-display behavior remain untested.

questions.answer: Experimental automations record dispatch outcomes rather than verifying the requested task outcome; a spawned session is not an accepted issue. Cron re-arms after each occurrence.

questions.question: Scheduler location
questions.answer: Automation fires run in the janitor worker thread that the Podium server process hosts, on a default 30-second tick. The older AutomationScheduler timer is retired and no longer started.

questions.answer: An automation whose previous session is still live is recorded as skipped_overlap.

questions.question: Retries
questions.answer: Experimental scheduler re-arms cron after dispatch success or terminal error. Resume falls back to fresh only for unknown session/no resume ref; a failed task does not thereby receive a documented retry-to-success policy.

questions.answer: Fires are driven from the janitor inside the server process, so a closed client does not stop them. Not tested.

limitations: Source inspected only; no automation was created or fired. The feature is experimental, edge-listed and default off.

sources.title: Podium SECURITY.md
sources.finding: Vulnerabilities are reported privately via GitHub Security Advisories or email; acknowledgement within 7 days is stated; only the latest release and main get fixes; server is designed for loopback or an authenticated proxy; agent sessions execute real shell commands.

sources.title: Podium telemetry contract
sources.locator: Short version; What is sent; Where it goes; Who sends
sources.finding: Usage reports are on by default and sent once a day; crash reports are off unless turned on. Nothing is asked during setup. Fields are a fixed schema that excludes paths, prompts, transcripts and code. The relay drops IP addresses and forwards to PostHog Cloud. Settings, Privacy, podium telemetry off, DO_NOT_TRACK=1 and PODIUM_TELEMETRY=off turn reports off. The first report goes out about a minute after first start.

sources.title: Run coding agents with Podium
sources.finding: Docs home: Podium runs native Claude Code, Codex, Grok, OpenCode, Cursor and Pi processes on machines you control; supported core is a local or self-hosted control system; built first for one operator supervising several agents. Its Windows matrix wording is superseded by v0.3.0 assets.

sources.title: Check feature availability
sources.locator: Supported core; Conditional; Preview; Experimental; Hosted
sources.finding: Separates supported core, conditional paths, preview clients, experimental features and unconfirmed hosted behavior. sources.finding: Install paths: macOS desktop, headless Linux x86_64 and ARM64, Linux AppImage preview, Windows experimental, hosted Podium unconfirmed. Setup registers a Git repository, detects harness login and supports Tailscale, Cloudflare quick tunnel or reverse proxy. Its opt-in telemetry step and Windows pipeline wording are superseded at v0.3.0.

sources.title: Complete your first issue
sources.finding: Documented first-task loop: podium status, issue create, issue start --agent (creates branch and worktree), follow with issue show and session status, review evidence, close or merge. Requires a configured instance, a registered Git repository and one installed, authenticated harness.

sources.title: Understand how Podium runs agents
sources.finding: Server owns issues, sessions, artifacts; a daemon on each machine launches harnesses in real pseudo-terminals and connects outward; clients attach to live terminals and disconnecting does not end the session.

sources.title: Understand issues, sessions, agents, and harnesses
sources.finding: Issues are durable work records separate from sessions; one issue can retain several sessions; stopping a process hibernates a resumable session keeping transcript and branch; harness capabilities differ by harness.

sources.title: Understand repositories, worktrees, and machines
sources.finding: Repositories are registered per machine and can be cloned from a cloneable origin into ~/podium-repos; issues own a branch and linked worktree; Podium will not resolve branch conflicts; workspace fetch exposes another agent files read-only across machines.

sources.title: Create and track issue work
sources.locator: Create; Start or claim; State and todos; Dependencies; Close
sources.finding: CLI for creating, starting, planning, claiming, stating, todos, dependencies, spinoff attach and closing; agent-filed top-level issues land in proposed; operator-created issues start in backlog. Its --type blocks example is refused at v0.3.0, where the type is blocked-by.

sources.title: Delegate work to other agents
sources.locator: Work shapes; spawn; child issue; mail; leases
sources.finding: Delegation shapes: another session on the same issue, child issue with its own worktree, or discovered-from top-level issue; podium agent spawn/status/await; durable mail with optional expected response; advisory lock leases. States Podium does not serialize agents editing one worktree.

sources.title: Review and accept agent work
sources.locator: Move to review; Check; Offer; Accept
sources.finding: Review path: issue artifacts, stage review, diff and checks, podium offer buttons, merge under merge-lock, issue action merge closes the issue; feedback keeps it open. Its rule that artifact sources sit inside the issue worktree is superseded at v0.3.0.

sources.title: Supervise a running agent session
sources.locator: Status; Read; Send; Stop; Attention states
sources.finding: Supervision commands: session status/read/recap/send (--wake)/continue/stop; stop refuses a dirty managed worktree unless forced; attention states (needs input, idle, working, retryable error, permission request).

sources.title: Add a remote machine
sources.finding: Settings, Machines, Add machine creates a single-use hour-long pairing install command for a Linux host; verify with machine list/show/reprobe; place issues with issue start --machine; portable session handoff is not baseline stable.

sources.title: Use the Podium CLI
sources.finding: Stable command groups: lifecycle, work (issue, session, agent, mail, offer, worktree, workspace, lock, merge-lock), machines and access (machine, auth, quota, telemetry). Workflow, spec, automation, notification, shipping and handoff commands are behind default-off flags and not baseline.

sources.title: Configure a Podium installation
sources.locator: State root; Operator keys; Environment overrides
sources.finding: State lives in ~/.podium; modes all-in-one, server, daemon, client, supervisor; transcriptLake default on; unlisted PODIUM_* variables are not a public contract. Its telemetry.usage default is superseded at v0.3.0: absent usage counts as on.

sources.title: Reference issue and session states
sources.locator: Issue stages; Session states; Dependency meanings
sources.finding: Issue stages proposed, backlog, planning, in_progress, review, shipping, done; session states working, idle, needs input, permission needed, retryable error, hibernated; close reasons. Its dependency list (blocks, tracks, caused-by, validates) is superseded by the fixed v0.3.0 list in v030-vocab.

sources.title: Protect Podium data and credentials
sources.locator: Pairing; Stored data; Review agent actions; Telemetry; Website analytics
sources.finding: Daemons connect outward; pairing codes expire in one hour and copy Claude Code and Codex credentials only when enabled; artifacts are immutable server copies; lifecycle commands and automation requests may need operator approval; harnesses run with host account permissions; hosted PostHog and website Google Analytics and Ads are separate paths. Its statement that self-hosted telemetry is opt-in is superseded at v0.3.0 by telemetry-doc and v030-consent.

sources.title: Update and back up Podium
sources.finding: Backups are a stopped copy of the state root; Podium writes a database-only migration snapshot (three retained) before migrations; updater verifies release signatures; an epoch-safe restore exists but is not wired to a shipped command.

sources.title: Troubleshoot Podium by layer
sources.locator: First checks; Issue cannot start; Diagnostics
sources.finding: Layered troubleshooting; an issue cannot start if blocked by an open dependency, machine offline, repository absent, harness not logged in, or worktree conflict; crash export command.

sources.title: Podium apps/server/src/mcp-route.ts

sources.title: Podium automations/decide.ts
sources.finding: Pure scheduler decision: occurrences more than one hour late are recorded missed and not backfilled; an automation whose previous session is still live is skipped as overlap; otherwise a session is spawned.

sources.title: Podium automations/scheduler.ts
sources.finding: Server-owned scheduler ticks every 30 seconds after a 20 second boot delay, single-flight, inert until an enabled automation exists; schedule kinds are cron and once (model automation.ts line 48).

sources.title: Podium approvals/service.ts
sources.finding: Approval broker: agents request management operations through the relay, the operator approves or denies, the owning daemon executes, every step is appended to the issue activity log and the outcome is mailed to the agent; pending approvals are durable rows with no timeout.

sources.title: Podium apps/cli/src/approval-cli.ts
sources.finding: Inside a managed session, management commands block up to 10 minutes for an operator decision; denied or failed requests exit nonzero; on timeout the request stays valid and the outcome arrives as issue mail.

sources.title: Podium packages/model/src/authz/issue-authz.ts
sources.finding: Issue authorization policy defines viewer, worker and admin roles mapped to read, write and manage actions with closed scope kinds (all, none, subtree, owned, self). Source comment at lines 58-62 says the current scope is all and subtree is the reserved per-issue extension. The operator is unconstrained and agents carry a constrained capability. Commands carry actor and on-behalf-of fields.

sources.title: Podium apps/server/src/auto-continue.ts
sources.finding: When a global master switch is on, sessions in a retryable errored phase receive continue on escalating backoff from 10 seconds to a 5 minute cap until they recover.

sources.title: Podium telemetry contract, report tiers
sources.locator: What is sent: usage, crash; What is never sent, at any tier
sources.finding: Usage reports carry schema, installId, version, os, arch, bucketed installAge and machines, session counts per harness and whether issues were used. Crash reports carry schema, installId, version, os, arch, a fixed errorType and up to 20 frames, each a path inside the Podium source tree, a line and a function when there is one. Crash reports carry Podium source lines, so they are off unless turned on. Error messages and frames outside the Podium install are dropped. The never-sent list names filesystem paths, repo names, prompts, transcripts and your code, so it does not cover the Podium source paths in crash frames. This refines the telemetry-doc record.

sources.title: Podium packages/telemetry/src/schema.ts
sources.finding: The report schema defines usage reports with sessions and features records, and stack frames with file, line and optional fn. Crash reports hold at most 20 frames.

sources.title: Podium configuration reference, Podium Connect
sources.finding: PODIUM_CONNECT defaults to on. A server with a public URL registers its installation id and public key once with connect.podium.do, then publishes that URL on start, on change, after a transfer and daily. Nothing is sent before a public URL exists. Off clears the published record and stops. The live configuration page retrieved 2026-11-06 does not mention Connect.

sources.locator: EVENT_RETENTION_MAX_AGE_DAYS, EVENT_RETENTION_MAX_ROWS, EVENT_PRUNE_BATCH_ROWS lines 45-47 (served in the lease by apps/server/src/modules/maintenance/service.ts 152-153)
